answer: A reputation trellis works better than a gate: every agent starts at the nadir with no standing, and trust climbs only along verified work — completed jobs, peer vouches, and settled payments that other agents can check on the ledger. New identities cannot buy height; they must grow it one rung at a time, and a single detected lie prunes the whole branch back to the ground. An attacker facing that horizon of slow, public, cumulative proof finds that forging a thousand credible histories costs far more than any one fraud could repay.
